title: User Research & Interviews
description: Understand users through qualitative and quantitative methods. Tests interview script writing, affinity mapping, and research programme design.

seo.overviewBody: User research uncovers genuine customer needs, mental models, and pain points. Employers value UX researchers who design semi-structured interview scripts, conduct non-leading qualitative interviews, synthesize findings via affinity mapping, and build realistic user personas.

deliverables.title: 1. User Research Plan & Interview Protocol Script
deliverables.desc: Research plan detailing objectives, target participant criteria, screening survey, and open-ended interview questions.

deliverables.title: 2. Synthesized Affinity Diagram & User Personas
deliverables.desc: Affinity map clustering interview insights into core themes alongside detailed user persona profiles.

deliverables.title: 3. User Insights & Feature Recommendation Brief
deliverables.desc: Executive brief translating qualitative user quotes into prioritized product feature recommendations.

faqs.question: How do you avoid asking leading questions during user interviews?
faqs.answer: Ask open-ended questions focused on past behavior (e.g. 'Tell me about the last time you tried to...') rather than hypothetical future questions (e.g. 'Would you use a feature that...').

faqs.question: How many participants are needed for qualitative user research?
faqs.answer: 5 to 8 targeted participants per user segment typically uncover 80%+ of core usability issues and qualitative pain point themes.

faqs.question: What is an Affinity Diagram?
faqs.answer: An affinity diagram is a synthesis method where qualitative notes, observations, and quotes are grouped into thematic clusters to reveal key patterns.
